subtopics: Probability distributions, expectation and binomial models
html:
A random sample of 150 households within a large town revealed that 48 households owned a cat, 60 owned a dog and 27 owned both a cat and a dog. You may assume that point estimates of probabilities derived from this sample are reliable and representative of the whole town.

  1. For households within the town, determine the probability that

  2. a randomly selected household owns neither a cat nor a dog. (2 marks)

  1. in a random sample of 5 households, exactly 3 will not own a dog. (2 marks)

  2. in a random sample of 9 households that own a dog, at least 2 will own a cat. (3 marks)

  1. If another random sample of 276 households was drawn from within the town, determine the mean and standard deviation of the probability distribution that models the number of households that own either a cat or a dog in the sample. (3 marks)
answerHtml: Supplied worked solution and marking criteria
text: A random sample of 150 households within a large town revealed that 48 households owned a cat, 60 owned a dog and 27 owned both a cat and a dog. You may assume that point estimates of probabilities derived from this sample are reliable and representative of the whole town. For households within the town, determine the probability that a randomly selected household owns neither a cat nor a dog. (2 marks) in a random sample of 5 households, exactly 3 will not own a dog. (2 marks) in a random sample of 9 households that own a dog, at least 2 will own a cat. (3 marks) If another random sample of 276 households was drawn from within the town, determine the mean and standard deviation of the probability distribution that models the number of households that own either a cat or a dog in the sample. (3 marks)

html:
A hire company has a fleet of nn scooters in a city. On any given day, the probability that one of their scooters needs a repair is independent with a constant value of pp. The daily number XX needing a repair has a mean of 31.68 and standard deviation 5.28.

  1. Determine nn and pp. (3 marks)

  2. The daily repair cost CC, in dollars, consists of a fixed $750 plus an average of $27.50 per scooter repaired. Determine the mean and standard deviation of the daily repair cost. (2 marks)

66 mg of a radioisotope with a half-life of 99 hours was injected into a patient before a CT scan. The mass remaining after tt hours is M=M0e−ktM=M_0e^{-kt}.

  1. Determine M0M_0 and kk. (3 marks)

  2. Determine the mass remaining exactly 10 days after the injection. (1 mark)

  3. Eventually the remaining mass falls to 5.5 mg. (i) Determine how long after the injection this occurs. (2 marks) (ii) Determine the rate at which the radioisotope is changing at this time. (2 marks)
